say.never: A robot has only one claw, so the whole program must share the same one. Two things make that happen. A `private` constructor means nobody else can write `new ClawSubsystem()`. And `getInstance()` hands out the one copy, building it the first time it's asked.
say.bit: A singleton: private constructor plus `getInstance()` that builds the single copy on first use.

say.bit: The whole robot must share **one** shooter. A private constructor stops anyone writing `new`, and `getInstance()` hands out the single copy.
